title: 5. MANAGEMENT OF NAUSEA AND VOMITING IN PREGNANCY AND HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM:

blocks.content:
5. MANAGEMENT OF NAUSEA AND VOMITING IN PREGNANCY AND HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM:

NVP = 90 % of pregnancies.

Onset before 16 weeks

HG = 0.3 – 3.6% (Severe form of NVP)

Mechanism:

Hypersensitivity to vomiting hormone growth differentiation factor 15 IGDF – 15

HCG

Genetic predisposition.

Diagnosis of NVP

Onset: 4 -7 weeks

Peak: 9 weeks.

Settles: 20 weeks in 90% women.

Rule out other causes.

Onset must be before 16 weeks.

Onset after 10+6 weeks => less likely NVP.

HG:

Severe NVP affecting daily activity

Inability to eat or drink

Dehydration.

Ketonuria is no longer used

Severity of NVP

1.Objective and validated index

2.PUQE SCORE

PUQE index also track response to treatment for mild & moderate but not severe and HG

3.HELP – can be used to track response to treatment in severe NV and HG.

PUQE score(24HRS):

Mild = up to 6.

Moderate = 7 – 12.

Severe = 13 – 15.

Patient with NVP or HG:

Exclude other causes

Record PUQE

Assess for complications

Dehydration

Weight loss

Electrolyte imbalance

Support + Advice

 

 

Management:

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Recommended antiemetic therapies and dosages

 

 

IMPORTANT POINTS REGARDING ANTIEMETICS

Pyridoxine NOT recommended

Steroid – where std therapies fails.

Diazepam – NR.

Ginger – in mild – moderate who wish to avoid antiemetics.

Accustimulation safe & improve NVP.

Hypnosis – NR.

Extrapyramidal S/E – with metoclopramide and phenothiazine (slow I/V injection over 3 min)

Combination is offered if no response to one drug

I/V Antiemetics:

After specialist advice

In the following patients:

Epilepsy

Psychiatric conditions

Hypoadrenalism

HIV

HG increases risks in followings:

DM

Gastric band

Gastric bypass

Gastric sleeve surgery

 

Fluids:

Normal saline 9% with KCL guided by S/E monitoring.

Dextrose infusions avoided until

S/Na+ - is normal.

Thiamine replaced.

It can precipitate Warnicke encephalopathy

Appropriate for NV in 3rd trimester to treat and prevent starvation ketosis.

Monitoring:

Urea/Electrolytes daily who require I/V fluids

Supportive Therapies:

H2 Antagonists or PPI => in GERD, esophagitis, Gastritis.

Thiamine

Thiamine: dose 100mg, P/O, three times a day or I/V pabrinex as part of B – complex

Indications of thiamine:

before dextrose

before parental Nutrition.

all women admitted with vomiting.

Severely reduced dietary intake

HG

Thromboprophylaxis – LMWH:

Those who are managed in community setting should be assessed for risk of VTE

Discontinue thromboprophylaxis upon discharge or continue if there is any other indication

Iron: avoid if they cause exacerbation of symptoms.

Laxatives: if constipated or using ondansetron

Complications & t/m:

GRED – Gastroscopy is safe, PPI can be used.

WERNICKES encephalopathy – reversible, potentially fatal medical – emergency B1 deficiency.

Symptoms = confusion, memory loss, drowsiness, Blurred vision.

O/E = Nystagmus, Ophthalmoplegia, Hypo/Areflexia, Finger nose ataxia

In HG there is episodic and slow onset.

Effect of NVP and HG on Mental Health:

Pre – existing conditions are exacerbated particularly with HG where prescribed medication is not kept down

HG is a risk factor or PSTD, PND anxiety.

Recommendation:

Proactive use of antiemetics and alternate

Routes of drugs.

Appropriate assessment and referral

Support group referral

(pregnancy sickness support).

Discharge and ongoing ANC:

Complete remission :29%

Discharge when:

Antiemetics are tolerated

Hydration is tolerated

Nutrition is optimum

Management of current condition is completed.

Readmission in 1/3rd women

Complication of HG:

Pre – term birth

Low birth weight

IUGR:

Autism

ADHD

Testicular cancer

IUGR –

Growth scan if vomiting continued after 20 weeks OR in late 2nd & 3rd.

Parenteral Nutrition TPN:

with MDT discussion

used as last resort

Complication of TPN

Refeeding syndrome.

MDT:

midwife nurse dietician, Pharmacist, endocrinologists’ nutritionist, Gastroenterologist, Mental health team.

TOP 10% of HG:

when all therapeutic options failed including parenteral nutrition after MDT discussion.

Reoccurrence:

15.2 – 8%.

Advice regarding diet & antiemetic’s that worked previously.
